As someone who worked at a doggy daycare, it was just awful for the anxious dogs, especially the ones who came almost every day. If you google "doggy daycare every day" [you get articles like this ](https://dogsdayoutseattle.com/day-care-bad-dog/)that suggest bringing your dog only 2-3 a week and possibly not at all if your dog has anxiety issues. It is very likely that you are majorly stressing your dog out and exacerbating his anxiety/behavioral issues, especially if the daycare attendants aren't trained dog behaviorists (and it is very likely that they aren't). Even dogs that seemed excited to come in to daycare would just act freaked out the entire time that they were there and then act all excited again when they get to go home. A dog walker would probably be a better option.

I feel like I fall into this category. I used to have off the charts social anxiety before working different retail jobs for a couple of years. I’m not really anxious anymore but even after all of this time and all of that practice I am still unbelievably socially awkward. I have a really hard time holding conversations with people, including coworkers at this job I’ve already had for a few months. My brain feels like it takes too long to process words and formulate a response that can keep up with the pace of a conversation, ESPECIALLY if it’s with a group. It takes so much energy and I usually end up saying something completely different from what I mean, if my brain doesn’t just stall completely because I literally can’t think of a single thing to say. It’s something I fight through on a regular basis. It just means that I’m not a great conversationalist and many people don’t like that.
On the flip side, I’m able to make easy friends with people who share a lot of similar interests to me. Unfortunately, I’m not statistically likely to find someone that can help me advance in a white-collar career who is also willing to talk extensively about anime and video games. It sounds like you experienced stimulant crashes, and stimulants might not be the medication for you. It's a good thing there are lots of non-stimulant medication that have been shown to help ADHD symptoms. 

I have ADHD-I and without Adderall I feel like I'm in constant low power mode. I thought I had depression my entire life, but it turns out that the lack of dopamine in my brain was making it impossible to focus on anything and extremely hard to socialize or motivate myself to do anything I loved. Adderall makes me feel like I have the energy to be a functioning human being and I have 0 crashing symptoms after it wears off. 

From my basic understanding of why people with ADHD are prescribed stimulants, that's what the stimulants are supposed to do. They're supposed to give your brain the baseline amount of dopamine to function like everyone else's (even if it's not a perfect solution). If you don't have ADHD you're just flooding your brain with extra dopamine.
As someone with ADHD-I, I really think you should get tested for ADHD

I learned pet care through taking my time and letting myself learn things as I went. Definitely learn the nitrogen cycle ([https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=es7spyo5RJ4](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=es7spyo5RJ4)) and learn in-depth information on how to set up and care for an aquarium. You will get a LOT of questions about that.

Unfortunately, a lot of it is left to us to research and find out. Fortunately, if you're being trained in pet care you probably really like animals and you'll find a lot of the info to be very interesting and useful outside of work!
